winter.why: Word of a full granary has gone down the valley.

question.text: Bring every soul and the granary to the thaw.

chronicle.text: The other 84 nights of winter went by routine, the wall stood in turns.
The thaw brought down the west wall where it was climbed all winter. It cannot be stood next winter.
A hungry spring: the granary could not reach the harvest, and everyone went short until it came. Yunus gave away half of every bowl and grew thin.
Oren and Hana came up the valley with their child Ivo, fleeing a raid, and asked to stay. They live behind the mill wall.
A thin harvest: the granary is half empty going into winter.
The autumn fair came to the meadow below the Gate.
Masons from the fair raised the west wall again before the snow.
A bigger bell was hung over the Gate.
Seed grain was bought for next year.
You named Joss heir to the Gate, before Tamar had said a word.
Winter came. A hard frost has driven the packs down early. Bring every soul and the granary to the thaw.
Hana and Oren are expecting a child.
Not done: Bring every soul and the granary to the thaw.
The rest of the winter, 82 nights, passed in turns on the wall: cold, dark and uneventful. Hana and Yunus took the most turns.
Rebuilt by the masons, the west wall was still climbed 15 times this winter.
Joss, named heir at the fair, never stood the Gate this winter. The Gate is learned on the Gate.
Oren and Hana and the child left with the thaw, down the valley road. Their house stands empty.
Oren and Hana left: the first household to go.
A hungry spring: the granary could not reach the harvest, and everyone went short until it came. Yunus gave away half of every bowl and grew thin.
A good harvest: the granary is well filled.
The autumn fair came to the meadow below the Gate.
The west wall was raised and lengthened: a third post there now.
Winter came. Word of a full granary has gone down the valley. Bring every soul and the granary to the thaw.
Done: Bring every soul and the granary to the thaw.
For 83 nights nothing came worth the lantern. The watch changed at midnight and the snow kept falling. Joss and Kian were on the wall more nights than anyone.
Raised at the fair, the west wall was still climbed 14 times this winter.
Joss and Mara and the children left with the thaw, down the valley road. Their house stands empty.
Yunus left with the thaw, down the valley road. Their house stands empty.
The thaw brought down the west wall where it was climbed all winter. It cannot be stood next winter.
Inge came up the valley alone and asked to stay.
Kian and Inge are seen walking out together.
Inge took sling lessons from Tamar in the summer evenings.
Kian would not have Inge.
Kian would not have Inge.
Kian would not have Inge, and you had spoken against it.
A thin harvest: the granary is half empty going into winter.
Kian would not have Inge.
Kian would not have Inge.
Kian would not have Inge.
The autumn fair came to the meadow below the Gate.
Cem and Yara and their child Petra were let in at the fair. They live behind the mill wall.
You named Kian heir to the Gate, before Tamar had said a word.

card.text: Inge has asked for Kian’s hand.
card.read: They have been walking out a long while; he looks glad of it.

lastVoices.joss: “I was glad not to be on the west wall.” “I wasn’t going to stand the mill wall.”
lastVoices.kian: “From the Gate I kept looking over at the west wall.”
lastVoices.mara: “Every sound from the Gate, I jumped.”
lastVoices.ruslan: “Every sound from the east wall, I jumped.”
lastVoices.tamar: “There’s something about the west wall. I can’t say what.” “I wasn’t going to stand the west wall.”
lastVoices.yunus: “I wasn’t going to stand the mill wall.”
